species.name: Crappie
why: Water 61°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 6–24 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 61°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 8–24 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
Southeast wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the northwest shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Walleye
why: Water 61°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.

The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
Southeast wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the northwest shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Largemouth bass
why: Water 61°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 4–18 ft deep, mostly on sheltered coves.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 55 ft, cold below.
Southeast wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the northwest shore: try the wind-blown banks.
